Optimal.Notes: A slight bump to medium textures and anti-aliasing over MaxBattery gives a noticeably cleaner image while FSR at 1024x640 keeps the GPU load manageable; Lumen must remain off. This profile targets a stable 30 fps cap with the 40 Hz refresh rate for reduced judder.

profiles.Summary: ARK: Survival Ascended is a demanding Unreal Engine 5 title whose PC minimum GPU requirement (RX 5600 XT / GTX 1080) already exceeds the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU by a significant margin, making stable performance a real challenge. With aggressive settings reductions, FSR upscaling, and a 30 fps target the game is playable, but expect compromises in visual quality and occasional dips in dense areas.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC system requirements (minimum GPU already exceeds the Deck's capability) and UE5 open-world game behaviour on the hardware. On first launch, check the frame-rate counter in an open outdoor area and reduce View Distance or render resolution further if you see sustained dips below 25 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Every setting is pushed to minimum and the render resolution is dropped to 960x600 with FSR to relieve GPU pressure; half-rate shading further cuts power draw. Even so, expect occasional dips below 30 fps in the most demanding outdoor areas.

KnownIssues: The game's UE5 Lumen and Nanite features are extremely demanding and should be disabled or set to minimum on Deck.
Long initial shader compilation stalls are expected on first launch.
Dense foliage areas, large bases, and many creatures on screen can cause significant frame drops below 30 fps.
The game requires a substantial SSD install (~180 GB) and may have longer-than-usual load times on slower storage.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 15 W TDP and maximum GPU clock squeeze every frame out of the hardware; even so, 60 fps is not realistically achievable on Deck with this title, so the cap stays at 30 fps. Shadows and foliage remain on Low because they are the biggest frame-rate killers in UE5 open-world games.

Optimal.Notes: A slight bump to texture and view distance quality over MaxBattery while still keeping Lumen and Nanite off; FSR at 1024x640 gives a reasonable image with the sharpness filter. Stable 30 fps is achievable in most open-world areas but expect occasional dips in busy multiplayer servers.

Battery life will be short and thermals will be at their peak — best suited for plugged-in or short sessions.
